name: Pakistan
summary: Created in 1947 at the partition of British India as a homeland for Muslims; East Pakistan broke away as Bangladesh in 1971; a nuclear power with long periods of military rule.

location.value: South Asia, between India, Iran, Afghanistan and China, on the Arabian Sea, covering about 882,000 km².

terrain.value: Indus plain, Karakoram and Himalaya, desert.

climate.value: Hot and dry in most of the country, with summer monsoon rains and cold highlands in the north.

resources.value: Farmland irrigated by the Indus, natural gas, coal and cotton.

disasters.value: Earthquake in Kashmir (2005), and floods in 2010 and 2022, which affected tens of millions of people.

population.value: About 240 million people (2023 census), the fifth-largest population in the world.

urbanisation.value: Karachi is the largest city and financial centre; Lahore is the cultural capital.

disease.value: Pakistan is one of the last places with wild polio, and malaria and dengue are widespread.

migration.value: Partition in 1947 caused the largest mass migration in human history: about 6.5 million Muslims moved from India to West Pakistan and 4.7 million Hindus and Sikhs moved to India.

economicBase.value: Farming, textiles and money sent home by workers abroad.

tradeRoutes.value: Seaports such as Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, linked to China by the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.

wealth.value: A lower-middle-income country, with a large informal economy and heavy debt.

moneyAndTax.value: The Pakistani rupee; taxes are collected from a small share of the population.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A federal parliamentary republic, with four provinces and several territories.

keyRulers.value: Muhammad Ali Jinnah. Ayub Khan. Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. Benazir Bhutto. Pervez Musharraf.

succession.value: Governments have been changed by elections and by military coups (1958, 1977, 1999).

institutions.value: The army holds great influence, and the parliament and courts have often clashed with it.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Underground nuclear tests in 1998 made Pakistan the seventh country to possess nuclear weapons.

majorWars.value: Wars with India in 1947–48, 1965 and 1971; the 1971 war ended with East Pakistan becoming Bangladesh.

territoryChange.value: East Pakistan broke away as Bangladesh in 1971; Kashmir remains disputed with India.

alliancesRivals.value: Close to China and Saudi Arabia, with a long rivalry with India and an on-off partnership with the United States.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Abdus Salam won a Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the electroweak interaction.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: An inter-provincial motorway network and the Karakoram Highway; Lahore’s Orange Line Metro opened in 2020.

languageWriting.value: Urdu and English; Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, Balochi.

artsArchitecture.value: Qawwali music, truck art, Mughal buildings such as the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, and Urdu poetry.

socialStructure.value: A diverse society: the largest language groups are Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi and Saraiki speakers (2023 census).

dailyLife.value: Many families eat biryani, roti and chai, and large extended families often live together.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Pakistan continues as an independent state.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
